faq.a: Shahla is associated with the Arabic form شَهْلَا, whose core sense is shahla; having dark eyes with a bluish tinge.

faq.q: What is the origin of Shahla?
faq.a: Shahla is associated with Arabic. Shahla is Arabic شَهْلَاء (Shahlāʾ), describing eyes with a bluish tinge, used as a female given name.
Yes — the underlying form شَهْلَا is Arabic.
Shahla can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Shahla should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Shahlāʾ is not a Quranic personal name.
